about: Ranking gold set for W2a (PHASE2_PLAN.md Block B1). One pair is one query plus one passage that query must retrieve. Built by mining what Phase 1 already proved rather than by authoring from scratch, and every pair records which seam it came from so the aggregate can never be read as one homogeneous number.
on_the_assertion: A pair asserts `expect_doc` AND `expect_text_contains`, never a chunk_id. Chunk ids are not stable across a re-ingest: `africa-03-periplus-adulis` was re-chunked on 2026-08-13 (A4's Wikisource recovery of Periplus 4-6), and the Greek exports sentence the archived answers name as `original::002` now lives in `original::005`. A pair keyed on the id would, after re-ingest, silently measure ranking against the wrong passage - the doc-id-proxy failure this repository has already paid for once. `observed_chunk_id` is recorded as provenance only; the checker reports whether it survived and never asserts on it.
on_provenance: `archived_answer` pairs are mined from chunks retrieval itself returned, so they cannot contain the case where retrieval missed a passage entirely. Their recall is partly true by construction and the checker reports every metric per cohort as well as in aggregate. `retrieval_probe` and `translation_case` pairs were written against the material, not against a ranking, and are the cohort that can actually surprise. Query-to-target lexical overlap is recorded per pair in every ranking run rather than minimised: for a short English object description a faithful, unambiguous question necessarily shares vocabulary with it, and forcing the overlap down produces contrived or ambiguous queries. Read the authored cohort's recall next to its overlap.

cohorts.archived_answer: question -> a chunk an archived answer quoted, verified by cite.py. eval/answer_runs/.
cohorts.retrieval_probe: eval/gold/retrieval_probes.json - query and expected document authored in Part 6 with a stated rationale.
cohorts.translation_case: eval/gold/translation_cases.json - the passage was already chosen; the query is written here to reach it.
cohorts.authored: written in Block B against a document with no Phase 1 query of its own. NOT yet ruled on by the project owner.

non_english.note: Mirrors retrieval_probes.json. Used so an English query cannot be satisfied by an English translation, which would make a cross-lingual pair a same-language pair wearing a cross-lingual label.

excluded.antikythera: 'When was the Antikythera mechanism built?' is 15 of the 77 archived runs and has no known-good passage - it is the correctly-refused off-corpus question. recall@6, MRR@10 and score gap are all undefined without a known-good, so it is not a ranking pair. It belongs to the W4 answer gold set, where refusal is the assertion.

pairs.query: How did Chinese sources describe the Roman empire?
pairs.note: The hero demo for Classical Chinese retrieval. Asserts 大秦國一號犁靬, the opening of the verbatim Sanguozhi text now in original_text_excerpt. UNTIL 2026-08-22 THIS PAIR ASSERTED 大秦國一號犂靬 - 犂 not 犁 - and carried a note saying it deliberately asserted 'the characters that are on disk, not the characters that ought to be', because the record's excerpt was known corrupt against Chen Shou 1975 (PROGRESS.md, Da Qin block s4). The excerpt turned out to be not corrupt but invented: none of its three fragments occurs in the source. When it was replaced this assertion matched nothing and the pair silently left the run - pairs 33 -> 31, units 30 -> 29, and every aggregate moved because the DENOMINATOR shrank, not because retrieval changed. The workaround is retired; the assertion now tracks a sourced text.

pairs.query: Which African king says he made travel safe as far as Leuke Kome?
pairs.source_ref: Written in the same commit as data/seed_corpus/subsaharan_africa/adulis-throne.json, per ruling 54.
pairs.note: RULING 54, and the first pair in this project written under it. FINDING 43 recorded that F3 added six records, wrote no pairs for any of them, and the only measured effect of the tranche on retrieval was three older pairs moving down -- a tranche that adds competition and no queries makes the measurement worse as the corpus gets better. This pair is written BEFORE the record has been ranked, in the commit that adds the record, because a pair written after the run is a pair written knowing the rank. The anchor is `Λευκῆς κώμης`, which is in this record's Greek and in no other chunk of this corpus; the English `Leucê Cômê` is McCrindle's spelling and is not asserted, so the pair cannot be satisfied by reaching the translation chunk instead.

pairs.query: Which Nubian king called himself basiliskos in a Greek inscription?
pairs.source_ref: Written in the same commit as data/seed_corpus/subsaharan_africa/silko-talmis.json, per ruling 54.
pairs.note: RULING 54. The anchor βασιλίσκος Νουβάδων is in this record's Greek and in no other chunk of this corpus. The query uses the ROMANISED 'basiliskos' rather than the Greek, deliberately: it is an English query against a Greek target, which is the cross-lingual case this gold set exists to measure, and a query carrying the Greek string would be testing lexical overlap rather than retrieval. Written before the record was ever ranked.

on_units: Block C ruling 1 (BLOCK_C_RULINGS.md): a query with several acceptable targets is ONE scored unit, scored on its best acceptable target, with per-unit COVERAGE - how many of its targets reached the top 6 - reported beside it and never gated. Two units are multi-target: `muziris-cargo` (3 pairs) and `china-describes-rome` (2). The unit is declared, not inferred from identical query strings, because a denominator inferred from text nobody declared changes the moment a query is edited by a character; the loader asserts both directions - one unit means one query text, and pairs sharing a query text must share a unit. Cost of the ruling, to be printed beside any G2 number: `muziris-cargo-akananuru` at rank 309 is the corpus's one genuinely broken cross-lingual link and no longer counts toward the gate.
on_aligned_alternates: Block C ruling 2: a pair carrying `accept_aligned_translation` also accepts its document's own published translation of the SAME section - a correct answer to an English query, and not what the pair was written to refuse. Landing on a NEIGHBOURING section is still a miss, which is the discrimination tc-frankincense-harvest was authored to make. The alternate is computed at scoring time by answer.align.pair_chunks and is never written down here: a hand-copied alternate is a second copy that drifts from the record it came from, which is the same failure as keying on a chunk id. Accepted only where that module reports the alignment ground as 'section'; the ground is recorded per pair in every run. Cross-lingual reach is measured instead by the `lang_pool: non_english` probes, where an English translation cannot satisfy the pair by construction.
